prompt:
Replace the legacy flat filter parser with the routing expression language described below. Keep `routing.parse(text)`, `routing.matches(ast, record)`, and `routing.ParseError`. `ParseError` subclasses ValueError and has integer attribute `pos`, a zero-based character offset in the original Python string. Error message text is not prescribed.

Grammar: expression := or_expr; or_expr := and_expr ('||' and_expr)*; and_expr := unary ('&&' unary)*; unary := '!' unary | '(' expression ')' | comparison; comparison := IDENT ('==' | '!=') STRING. Thus ! binds tighter than &&, which binds tighter than ||; binary operators associate left. Identifiers match ASCII [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*. Only space, tab, CR and LF are skipped outside strings. STRING is double-quoted, may be empty or contain Unicode, and recognizes exactly four escapes: backslash followed by double quote decodes to double quote; backslash followed by backslash decodes to backslash; backslash followed by lowercase n decodes to newline; backslash followed by lowercase t decodes to tab. Raw CR/LF inside strings and all other escapes are errors. Operator characters inside strings are ordinary characters. Entire input must be consumed; there are no comments, single-quoted literals or bare values.

Return tuples: ('eq', field, decoded_value), ('ne', field, decoded_value), ('not', child), ('and', left, right), ('or', left, right). `matches` evaluates those tuples against a mapping of string field names to string values, returns bool, and never mutates inputs. A comparison on a missing field is False for BOTH eq and ne; normal present values compare exactly and case-sensitively. Boolean operations have their usual meaning (so NOT of a missing-field comparison is True).

Lex the full input left-to-right before syntactic parsing. Lexical errors report the first offending character; unknown escapes report the backslash, raw line breaks report that line-break character, unterminated quoted strings (including dangling backslash at EOF) report the opening quote. After successful lexing, syntax errors report the unexpected token's starting offset, or len(text) if a required token is missing at EOF. Empty/whitespace-only input is a syntax error at len(text). All malformed expressions must raise ParseError, not unrelated exceptions. Keep the parser/evaluator separated so existing rule loading can use parsed tuples. Add tests for nesting, precedence, quoting and diagnostics.
